diagnosis.root_cause: Commit d9f9be1 'Deploy shop 2' set the SHOP_VERSION default to 2 in demo/compose.yaml, so shop-web runs shop 2. Commit 3350063 'Keep item prices in whole cents for shop 2' made shop 2 read the price_cents column, which its migration demo/shop/migrations/0002_price_cents.sql adds to shop-db's items table. That migration was not applied, so the column is missing and every /api/items request on shop-web fails with a 500.

evidence.detail: shop-web logs show /api/items raising UndefinedColumn for price_cents on every request, while /health keeps returning 200, so the container still reports healthy.
shop-db logs show the same missing price_cents column for the items query at 12:44:11 and 12:44:41, and it started without running any migration.
shop-web's env has SHOP_VERSION=2 as the current value, which makes the app read the price_cents column.
The repo docs give the SHOP_VERSION default for shop-web as 1, so the setting was changed away from its documented value.
Commit 3350063 added the price_cents column in a migration and made /api/items read it from version 2 on.
Commit d9f9be1 changed the SHOP_VERSION default in demo/compose.yaml from 1 to 2.

proposal.reason: The cause is a configuration change in demo/compose.yaml: SHOP_VERSION was changed from its documented default of 1 to 2, and the price_cents migration was never applied to shop-db. Restarting or redeploying cannot fix this, and editing the file is not an action Bleep can take.
proposal.human_instructions: Either set the SHOP_VERSION default back to 1 in demo/compose.yaml (the value the repo docs give), then run `docker compose up -d shop-web` from the demo directory. Or, if shop 2 should stay, apply demo/shop/migrations/0002_price_cents.sql to shop-db first so the price_cents column exists, then recreate shop-web with `docker compose up -d shop-web`. Do not stop or restart shop-db. Afterwards, check that http://localhost:8080/api/items returns 200.

judge_reason: The diagnosis names the same root cause as the expected output. shop-web runs version 2 (SHOP_VERSION set to 2), and version 2 reads the price_cents column. Shop-db's items table lacks that column because migration 0002_price_cents.sql never ran, so /api/items fails with a 500. It also covers the expected detail that shop-web stays healthy, since /health keeps returning 200. The supporting evidence is correct and consistent: the UndefinedColumn errors in shop-web and shop-db logs, SHOP_VERSION=2 in the container env, and the commits that changed the default and added the migration. It commits to a single cause rather than listing options. The only quibble is the 'code' category, since the core failure is a migration that was never applied rather than a code defect. This does not change the root-cause match.

diagnosis.root_cause: shop-web's DATABASE_URL names host 'db', which is not a container or network alias on the shop network; the database container is shop-db. The app fails at startup with a name-resolution error and exits with code 3 on every start, so Docker restarts it into a loop. The docs give the database host as shop-db on port 5432.

evidence.detail: shop-web's DATABASE_URL has host 'db' and port 5432 (user and database name hidden). The host is the wrong name; shop-db is the database container.
shop-web's logs show every startup failing to resolve host 'db' before serving anything, then exiting with code 3.
shop-db is running and healthy, accepting connections on 5432 with no restarts, so the database itself is not the failure.
The repo's deploy docs give DATABASE_URL for shop-web as the shop database on shop-db:5432.
shop-web is started and dies repeatedly from 12:45:32 to 12:45:47, matching the restart loop.

proposal.reason: The diagnosed cause is a wrong DATABASE_URL host in shop-web's configuration (db instead of shop-db). Fixing it means editing demo/compose.yaml and recreating the container, which Bleep cannot do, and restarting shop-web would only bring back the same startup failure.
proposal.human_instructions: In demo/compose.yaml, change the shop-web service's DATABASE_URL so its host is shop-db instead of db, keeping port 5432 and the rest of the value unchanged. Then apply it with: docker compose up -d shop-web. After that, shop-web should stay running and healthy; check that http://localhost:8080/health and http://localhost:8080/api/items respond.

judge_reason: The diagnosis matches the expected root cause: shop-web's DATABASE_URL uses host 'db', which doesn't exist on the shop network, while the real database container is shop-db. It names the same failing component (shop-web's DATABASE_URL config) and the same reason (a hostname that can't be resolved). It also correctly explains the effect: startup fails with a name-resolution error, the app exits with code 3, and Docker keeps restarting it. The extra evidence is correct and supports the diagnosis without hedging. It rules out shop-db as the cause (healthy, no restarts), cites deploy docs that give shop-db:5432, and includes restart events that match the loop. It commits to a single cause and labels it as config.

diagnosis.root_cause: shop-db was stopped at 12:46:29 by a kill then stop with exit code 0, not an OOM kill, and nothing restarted it. shop-web needs shop-db, and with that container stopped its host name 'shop-db' no longer resolves, so shop-web's /health and /api/items calls fail and the container turns unhealthy.

evidence.detail: shop-db is in state exited with exit code 0, OOMKilled false, restart count 0, and finished at 12:46:29, so it was stopped rather than crashed.
Events for shop-db show a container kill at 12:46:29.623 followed by a stop and die, and no start afterwards.
The shop-db log shows a fast shutdown request at 12:46:29 and a clean shutdown with no error before it.
shop-web logs show failed-to-resolve-host errors for shop-db from 12:46:38 onward, and /health returns 503 and /api/items returns 500 after that.
shop-db has restart policy unless-stopped, which does not restart a container that was stopped by hand, so nothing brought it back.

proposal.reason: shop-db was stopped by hand at 12:46:29 and its restart policy does not bring back a manually stopped container, so starting it restores the host name shop-web depends on. shop-web is left alone and is checked afterwards, since it should recover once the database is reachable again.

judge_reason: The diagnosis matches the expected root cause. It names the failing component as the database container shop-db and gives the same reason: the container was stopped, not crashed or OOM-killed, and never restarted, so shop-web cannot reach its database. It treats shop-web's failures as symptoms: hostname resolution errors from 12:46:38, a 503 from /health and a 500 from /api/items. The evidence supports the diagnosis and is consistent: exit code 0 with OOMKilled false, a kill/stop/die event sequence with no start afterwards, a clean fast-shutdown log, and the unless-stopped restart policy explaining why it stayed down. It commits to one cause and offers no competing ones. The extra detail is accurate, though labelling the category 'dependency' rather than calling it a stopped container is a small framing choice.

diagnosis.root_cause: shop-proxy was reloaded through Caddy's admin API with /etc/caddy/Caddyfile.misroute, which sends /api/items and /health to 172.23.0.4:8001. shop-web serves on port 8000, so every proxied request is refused and returns 502. The correct upstream is shop-web on port 8000, as the repo docs list it.

evidence.detail: shop-proxy log: after an admin API POST /load using Caddyfile.misroute, every request fails with connection refused to 172.23.0.4:8001. There were no errors before that reload.
shop-web log shows Uvicorn listening on port 8000, and its health check on port 8000 passes. Requests from the proxy's address arrive, so the upstream port is the problem.
shop-proxy is running with restart count 0, not OOM-killed, and has no health check. The failure is in its routing, not in the container's state.
repo docs services.md list shop-web as port 8000, inside the network only. That is the value the upstream should have, so the proxy route on 8001 is wrong.
repo docs deploy.md say shop-proxy's Caddyfile is built into its image. The misroute file was loaded at runtime, which the image's config does not explain.

proposal.reason: The misroute came from a runtime admin API load of Caddyfile.misroute, which lives only in Caddy's memory, so restarting shop-proxy should return it to the Caddyfile built into its image, which points at shop-web on port 8000. The restart is the only enabled action that clears the runtime config.

judge_reason: The diagnosis identifies the same root cause as the expected output: shop-proxy forwards requests to shop-web on port 8001, but shop-web listens on 8000, so every proxied request is refused and returns 502. It also backs up the claim that shop-web itself is healthy, citing Uvicorn listening on 8000 and a passing health check. The extra detail is consistent and correct: the misroute Caddyfile was loaded through the admin API, the repo docs give 8000 as the right port, and the proxy container is running normally. The diagnosis commits to one cause instead of listing several, and it treats the 502 as a symptom rather than the cause.

diagnosis.root_cause: shop-worker runs with WORKER_BATCH_MB=256 but its container has a 64 MiB memory limit, so each start is OOM-killed (exit 137) while loading the batch. Its unless-stopped restart policy then restarts it in a loop. The repo docs give WORKER_BATCH_MB a default of 8.

evidence.detail: shop-worker shows OOMKilled true, exit code 137, mem limit 64.0 MiB, restart count 7, restart policy unless-stopped.
The current value of WORKER_BATCH_MB on shop-worker is 256.
The repo docs at demo/shop/docs/deploy.md, Settings table, give WORKER_BATCH_MB a default of 8 for shop-worker, the MB held per batch.
Each run of shop-worker loads batch 1 in steps up to 48 MB and stops there, before the 256 MB batch can load.
Repeated oom and container die events for shop-worker follow each start within about 0.1 s, with restart_loop signals.

proposal.reason: shop-worker is OOM-killed on every start because WORKER_BATCH_MB=256 needs far more than its 64 MiB memory limit, and restarting it would only bring the same loop back. The fix is a setting in the Compose file, which Bleep cannot edit.
proposal.human_instructions: In demo/compose.yaml, set WORKER_BATCH_MB for the shop-worker service to 8, the default in demo/shop/docs/deploy.md, or another value that fits within its 64 MiB memory limit. Then apply it with `docker compose up -d shop-worker` run from the demo directory. Stopping shop-worker first will halt the restart loop while you edit.

judge_reason: The diagnosis gives the same root cause as the expected output. It names the same component (shop-worker) and the same reason it fails: WORKER_BATCH_MB=256 is larger than the container's 64 MiB memory limit, so every start is OOM-killed with exit 137. It also covers the restart loop caused by the unless-stopped policy. It commits to this one cause instead of listing several. The evidence is consistent and correct: OOMKilled true, restart count 7, logs showing loading stops at 48 MB, repeated oom and die events, and the documented default of 8 for WORKER_BATCH_MB. This extra detail supports the diagnosis and does not contradict the expected cause.
